471.t: Pearl Bailey at 2011 and the 7th and T jam spot
471.s: Cobb mentions playing with Pearl Bailey, then describes 7th and T where theater musicians jammed.
471.ch: Bostic, Washington clubs and arriving in New York
471.q: Pearl Bailey was before I left Washington. I had an opportunity to play with her in 2011. You know where that is? That’s on 15th Street. It’s a complex.

471.t: The Stagedoor, Tim's half-smokes and the Howard area
471.s: Cobb recalls the Stagedoor, Cecile's, Klors's rooming house, and Tim's hot dog stand.
471.ch: Bostic, Washington clubs and arriving in New York
471.q: Stagedoor, Cecile’s – that was there. That’s right across from the Howard. Guys used to go over there in a bar – right from the Stagedoor, right straight to the bar. Then they had pretty good food in there. Upstairs, across the alley, was a restaurant that sold soul food, I think. I think it might…

471.t: After hours at the Caverns with Blanche Calloway
471.s: He remembers the Caverns, Blanche Calloway running it, and meeting Ruth Brown there.
471.ch: Bostic, Washington clubs and arriving in New York
471.q: Let’s see. On the after-hours side, where was it? After hours in Washington. I don’t remember too much after hours in Washington. If there was, I probably wasn’t old enough to get in it. After hours in Washington. I can’t – I don’t have no comprehension of.

471.t: Other Washington venues: 2011, Colonnade and Turner's Arena
471.s: He lists 2011, the Blue Mirror, the Colonnade with Rick Henderson, and Turner's Arena.
471.ch: Bostic, Washington clubs and arriving in New York
471.q: I’m trying to think of some other places was around Washington that we could work. That place was, like you say, 15th – it was called what the number of the place was: 2313, I think it was. That was the name of it. No, no: 2011. 2011 was the name of the building and the club.

19.t: Back in Washington: U Street and the Jungle Inn with Kay Hedgeman
19.s: He goes looking for work on U Street and lands at the Jungle Inn run by Miss Lyles, accompanying singer Kay Hedgeman.
19.ch: U Street, Jelly Roll Morton, the youth band and the WPA
19.q: So we came back to Washington, and I think this would be 1936, somewhere around there... When you think back, you kind of forget exactly where they are chronologically, but it's around in the same time. But chronologically, one thing might have happened before the other. But I went up on U Street.…

19.t: Hired for the band at the Crystal Caverns
19.s: The most prestigious U Street nightclub, home of Cavernism, needs a pianist, and he joins an eight-piece show band.
19.ch: U Street, Jelly Roll Morton, the youth band and the WPA
19.q: Then I was offered this job at a place on Eleventh and U called... Then it was called the Crystal Caverns, which was where Tommy Miles' band had worked some years before. And Jimmy Mundy had written this very popular, or I would say famous tune of his called "Cavernism" that Earl Hines' band later…

101.t: Rick Henderson and Washington, D.C. memories
101.s: Howard Theater, Edwina's, Wolf Trap and Hot Dog Tim's half-smokes.
101.q: Rick Henderson was an old roommate in the Basie – in the Ellington band. Rick was at one time the leader of the Howard Theater band in Washington, D.C., on 7th and T [Streets, NW] – 7th and Wiltberger [Street, NW].

225.t: Indiana Avenue clubs and the Walker Theater
225.s: Johnson and Baker place the Cotton Club, Sunset Terrace and the Walker Theater, mainly a movie house to him.
225.q: No, but I knew that they were there, and I knew that there were interesting things happening there, both legal and illegal. [laughter]

509.s: Olivia's was top; Abart's paid well; the Bohemian Caverns were prestigious but low-paying; the Hollywood was fun.
509.q: Everyone wanted to do Olivia‘s. That was top, right. Okay. Abart‘s was pretty cool, as far as the money, right. Okay. Then the Caverns came, and see, I don‘t remember much about the Crystal Caverns, because they had shows and stuff. But when it went to the Bohemian Caverns I went in there for a…

67.s: Philadelphia had many clubs and shows, such as the Standard Theater and the Paradise Club, and Atlantic City was jumping.
67.ch: Philadelphia, New York and Sam Wooding in Europe
67.q: Philadelphia was very good. Very, very good. Many clubs with bands.

124.s: Camden had little to offer a big band; trains ran straight to Atlantic City.
124.q: Yeah. Camden was never -- You know, Jersey was just being built up. Go and take the train, you go straight to Atlantic City. You ride a train down to Atlantic City.

455.t: Booker T. Washington Hotel, Elnora's restaurant and Maceo Pinkard
455.s: Hinton and Budd recall the Eblon, hotel, Street's and Elnora's restaurant, and Pinkard's drugstore.
455.ch: Kansas City, Basie, Prez and Booker Pittman
455.q: Now they had built a place called the Booker T. Washington Hotel, right across from the Eblon Theater. You probably know that --

171.t: The Cherry Blossom and Vine Street's musicians' hotels and clubs
171.s: The Cherry Blossom was the old Eblon Theatre where Basie once played organ; the street had the Booker T. Washington Hotel and Kentucky Tavern.
171.q: E-b-l-o-n. Eblon. And you remember in the previous years, Basie and this guy, O'Taylor, used to play there. They played this accompanying music while the silent movie, or something, was showing. And Basie played the organ and this guy played the violin.
